Event-Based Gateway

General Concept: An Event-Based Gateway in BPMN is used to model branching based on events, where the process waits for one of several possible events to occur before continuing. It is used for event-driven decision points.

 

TaktX Implementation: In TaktX, Event-Based Gateways wait for one of several possible events (message, timer, signal, etc.) and route the process accordingly. The engine manages event subscriptions and variable scope, and resumes the process when an event is caught. Input mappings using FEEL expressions can be used to process event data.

Usage & Options in TaktX:
An Event-Based Gateway in TaktX allows you to:

  • Wait for one of several possible events (message, timer, signal, etc.) and route the process accordingly.
  • Configure event subscriptions and trigger handling for flexible process routing.
  • Use input mappings to process event data and determine routing.
  • Set up error handling for unmatched or incorrect events.
  • Monitor event handling and audit results via the TaktX client.
  • Use for event-driven process routing and flexible workflows.

 

Example: Customer Response or Timeout with Event-Based Gateway

 

This example shows a process where an Event-Based Gateway waits for either a customer reply (message) or a timeout (timer) and routes accordingly. This demonstrates event-driven process routing in TaktX.

Tips & Tricks:

  • Use event-based gateways for flexible, event-driven processes.
  • Document expected events and outcomes.
  • Test gateway behavior with different event scenarios.

Pitfalls:

  • Unmatched events will not trigger the process.
  • Incorrect event configuration can block the process.
